chapter: Sidemen, the Hampton years, race and money
title: Royalties: Carla Bley, Brubeck and Paul Desmond
summary: Argument about whether white jazz musicians do better; Johnson says the record business steals from everyone.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: I'll bet he does. I talked to a girl, Carla Blay, last week and she's written some nice tunes and all that. You know Carla, Paul's wife. [Formra]
Yeah, I know her.
And she's telling me that -- just in mechanical royalties from record sales, and from having a lot of covering records, she makes about $30,000 a year in royalties.
She's white.
Huh?
She's white.
It hasn't got anything to do with that.
Is that publishing or artist royalties? (inaudible.)
No, they're mechanical royalties. So --
(inaudible.) And she's not even on a major label.
No, she's not a major artist.

Well, all I know is, if Dizzy Gillespie Illinois Jacquet had a heart attack, Jackie and them would have $1,000. Now, that's -- I'm talking about black people, I ain't talking about white people. White people make money.
Do you know with the exception of Fantasy Records (inaudible.) you make more than I make in a one every year.
I bet he one every year.
Hm?
I bet you make more than I make a year.
I bet I don't, Charles. No way.
Do you know that Charles has never gotten (inaudible.) artist royalties with the exception of Fantasy Records, which is owned by a former wife?
I'm not surprised at that, but not many white jazz musicians get artists' royalties on their records.
Dave Brubeck did.

Yeah, but Brubeck sold millions of records. Brubeck couldn't swing his way out of a paper bag, but he was an enormous popular success. He sold millions of copies of those quartet records with of Paul Desmond.
What was that the attorney he said last night, Sue, that Paul Desmond didn't get much money?
He said that when he oversaw the latest (Inaudible) contract with Paul Desmond, Paul did start getting artist royalties and very quickly.

Yeah, but Paul never made very ambitious records. Talking about the things he was making with -- I mean, he made quartet records and stuff like that. And there's no budget involved. I mean, it depends on how much money it costs to produce the record. And every time -- I've never seen a royalty statement from anybody I know, white or black, that didn't -- that wasn't startling. It was one of those things where you wind up -- you owe Atlantic Records $50,000 for something like that. That's true of everybody. There are very few people who make enough money to ever get past that bookkeeping system that record companies have. And that has nothing to do with being black. That's just the way the record business -- they steal from everybody. They don't discriminate against anybody. They steal from anybody.
